clusters.title: Frequent Audio Drops During Huddles
clusters.summary: Users report mid-conversation audio cutouts that require leaving and rejoining the huddle to restore sound, often without any visual warning that audio has been lost. This disrupts team standups and paired programming sessions where continuity is critical.
verbatims: At least twice per standup my audio just vanishes — I'm still shown as active in the huddle but nobody can hear me. I have to leave and rejoin every single time, which breaks the flow of the whole meeting.

I've been doing paired coding sessions via Huddle and the audio drop issue is killing us. No error, no notification, just silence. My teammate thinks I'm ignoring them and I have no idea I've dropped.

The reconnect loop is what gets me — I leave the huddle to fix audio, Slack shows me as rejoining for 10 seconds, then dumps me back to a blank screen. Takes three tries sometimes just to get back in.

clusters.title: Screen Share Quality Unusable for Code Review
clusters.summary: Screen sharing inside Huddle renders at noticeably low resolution with 2-4 second lag, making text in code editors, terminals, and design tools illegible for remote participants. Developers and designers consistently report abandoning Huddle screen share in favor of Zoom or Meet for any detail-oriented work.
verbatims: I tried doing a code review in a Huddle and my teammate literally could not read the function names on their end — everything was pixelated. We gave up and jumped to Zoom mid-session. This is a daily workaround now.

The lag on screen share is so bad that when I'm walking through a Figma prototype, my mouse cursor is in a completely different spot than what viewers see. It makes live design walkthroughs basically impossible.

I don't understand how Teams and Zoom can share a 4K screen clearly and Huddle makes my terminal look like a JPEG from 2004. I use Slack all day and I really want to stay in it, but not for anything I actually need to show someone.

clusters.title: No Way to Schedule or Reserve Huddles
clusters.summary: Huddle is designed for spontaneous conversation with no native scheduling, calendar integration, or the ability to send a Huddle link in advance, forcing users to coordinate meeting times through separate messages and then manually start the Huddle at the right moment. Teams that mix async and synchronous work find this gap creates friction around recurring syncs and cross-timezone calls.
verbatims: My team does a Monday planning call every week and I have to post in the channel 'starting the Huddle now' every single time. There's no way to schedule it, no Google Calendar block, no reminder — it's 2024 and I'm herding people manually.

I want to send a Huddle link to an external contractor the way I'd send a Zoom link, but that doesn't exist. I end up using Zoom for anything planned and Huddle only when someone is already online. That's a huge limitation.

We use Slack Connect with a client and they asked me to set up a Huddle for our weekly check-in. I had to explain that I can't schedule it or send them a link ahead of time. They looked at me like I was joking. So did I, honestly.

clusters.title: Camera Feed Freezes Without Notification
clusters.summary: Participants' video feeds frequently freeze on a static frame while audio continues, and neither the sender nor the receiver receives any indicator that the video has stopped updating. This creates awkward interactions where users are responding to a frozen expression or a black square without realizing the feed failed.
verbatims: My camera froze on a really unflattering frame mid-huddle and I had no idea for like 5 minutes. My coworker finally typed in chat 'are you okay, you haven't moved.' There should at least be an indicator that your video is frozen.

I've started just turning my camera off entirely in Huddles because it freezes so often that it's more distracting than helpful. The audio is fine but the video just locks up, usually right after I share my screen.

Half the time when I join a Huddle I see frozen thumbnails of everyone's faces from the last time they were on camera. It looks like they're all there but then I realize none of the video tiles are actually live. Very confusing UX.

clusters.title: No Recording, Transcript, or Recap Feature
clusters.summary: Unlike competing tools, Huddle offers no built-in recording, automatic transcript, or AI-generated summary after a call ends, meaning any decisions or action items discussed verbally are immediately lost unless someone manually takes notes. Async-heavy and distributed teams flag this as a reason they cannot fully adopt Huddle as their primary voice communication tool.
verbatims: We made a whole set of sprint decisions in a Huddle and two people were async. I had to write up everything that was said from memory afterward. Every other tool we've tried at least records or summarizes. This is a dealbreaker for distributed teams.

Slack has AI features now for summarizing channels and messages — why does Huddle not get a transcript or even a basic 'here's what was discussed' after the call? I keep losing context from quick syncs because nothing is captured.

I love that Huddles are lightweight but the total lack of any record of what happened is a real problem. Even a simple thread in the channel that says 'Huddle ended, 3 participants, 14 minutes' with a transcript attached would change how my whole team uses this.
